mechanism_narrative: A lower federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is associated with higher S&P 500 60-day forward returns due to reduced discount rates on equity cash flows, as evidenced by the current near-zero rate environment.
evidence_refs: fact:Current FEDFUNDS at 0.16% is near zero, a level historically associated with positive equity returns
failure_condition: The Rank IC between FEDFUNDS and 60-day forward returns is less than 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A federal funds rate above 4.5% signals a monetary tightening cycle that increases discount rates on equity cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 5-day forward returns.
evidence_refs: fact:Current FEDFUNDS at 0.16% is below 4.5%, so the condition is not met
failure_condition: In more than 40% of periods when FEDFUNDS > 4.5%, the 5-day forward returns are non-negative.

mechanism_narrative: A combination of high unemployment (UNRATE > 8.5%) and rising employment (PAYEMS growth > 0.5% month-over-month) signals a stabilization in the labor market, leading to positive S&P 500 60-day forward returns as the Fed maintains accommodative monetary policy.
evidence_refs: fact:Current UNRATE=8.9% (above 8.5%) and PAYEMS increased from 130515.0 to 131057.0 (0.4% growth)
failure_condition: In more than 40% of periods meeting the trigger condition (UNRATE>8.5% AND PAYEMS growth>0.5% mo/m), the 60-day forward returns are non-positive.

mechanism_narrative: When unemployment rate (UNRATE) exceeds 8.0%, the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day forward returns due to expectations of monetary policy easing and economic recovery.
failure_condition: In more than 40% of periods when UNRATE > 8.0%, the 20-day forward returns are non-positive.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in industrial production (INDPRO) and housing starts (HOUST) signals robust economic activity, leading to positive S&P 500 5-day forward returns as the market prices in stronger corporate earnings.
evidence_refs: fact:Current INDPRO=93.4814 (falling from 95.1452) and HOUST=630.0 (rising from 596.0)
failure_condition: In more than 40% of periods when INDPRO and HOUST are both rising (growth > 0.5% mo/m), the 5-day forward returns are non-positive.

mechanism_narrative: Higher housing starts (HOUST) signal improving consumer confidence and economic activity, leading to positive S&P 500 60-day forward returns due to stronger housing sector and related economic growth.
evidence_refs: fact:Current HOUST=630.0 (above 500, so rising? but note: it's rising from 596 to 630)
failure_condition: The Rank IC between HOUST and 60-day forward returns is less than 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When housing starts (HOUST) fall below 500 thousand units, it signals a weakening housing market and economic slowdown, leading to negative S&P 500 5-day forward returns.
evidence_refs: fact:Current HOUST=630.0 (above 500, so condition not met)
failure_condition: In more than 40% of periods when HOUST < 500, the 5-day forward returns are non-negative.

mechanism_narrative: Rising industrial production (INDPRO) signals improving economic activity and corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
evidence_refs: fact:Current INDPRO=93.4814 (falling from 95.1452, so not rising)
failure_condition: The Rank IC between INDPRO and 20-day forward returns is less than 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.
